git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
Zoom out for the unknown-location fallback

Why:
When MusicBrainz has no origin for an artist we drop the bubble in the
Pacific at (0, -160). The fly-to used a fixed zoom 6 there, which framed
nothing but open water — it read like a broken tile layer instead of a
deliberate "we don't know where this artist is from".

How:
Tag PACIFIC_FALLBACK with `unknown: true` and have LeafletMap pick its
fly-to zoom via a new `zoomForLocation` helper: ARTIST_ZOOM (6) for a
resolved origin, UNKNOWN_ZOOM (3) for the fallback. At zoom 3 the
Americas and Oceania stay in frame, so the empty ocean is legible as a
nowhere rather than a rendering failure.

Tests:
New src/components/__tests__/LeafletMap.test.jsx covers both zoom
branches and asserts the unknown zoom stays wider than the artist zoom.
Full `npm test` via the pre-commit hook.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
I dug into the root cause with live API calls. Findings before I ask you two design calls:

- MusicBrainz gives Nirvana `begin-area: Aberdeen` (city) + `country: "US"`, but we send Nominatim the bare string `"Aberdeen"` → it returns Aberdeen, **Scotland** (highest "importance").
- Adding `countrycodes=us` alone isn't enough: it then returns Aberdeen, **South Dakota**.
- Fetching the area's parent from MusicBrainz (`/area/<id>?inc=area-rels` → `Grays Harbor County`) and querying `"Aberdeen, Grays Harbor County"` + `countrycodes=us` returns **46.975, -123.816 — Aberdeen, WA**. Correct.

So the fix needs one extra MusicBrainz hop per uncached artist (cached 180 days server-side, and skippable when the area is already a country).

questions.question: `src/geo.js` (browser, now-playing) and `server/geocode.js` (explore mode) are ~95% identical — the only difference is the throttle callbacks. This fix adds ~40 lines of non-trivial logic that both need, plus per-file coverage thresholds on both. How should I structure it?

options.label: Unify into one shared module (Recommended)
options.description: New `shared/geocode.js` holds the single implementation with optional throttle callbacks; `src/geo.js` and `server/geocode.js` go away, importers and both test suites point at the shared module. Fix lives in one place; needs a one-line coverage-include update in vite.config.js and a CLAUDE.md refresh.

options.label: Fix both files separately
options.description: Keep the current src/ vs server/ split untouched and implement the same disambiguation logic twice, with duplicated tests. Smaller blast radius, but the duplication (already there) doubles and the two can drift.

Unify the two copies of the geocoder into shared/geocode.js

Why:
src/geo.js (browser, now-playing) and server/geocode.js (explore mode)
were the same MusicBrainz -> Nominatim implementation twice over, down
to duplicated test suites; the only real difference was the optional
throttle callback. The place-name disambiguation work that follows adds
non-trivial logic both callers need, so fixing it twice — and keeping
two per-file coverage bars satisfied twice — is exactly the drift this
duplication invites.

How:
Moved server/geocode.js to shared/geocode.js (contents unchanged, the
superset already: throttle callbacks are optional) and deleted
src/geo.js. MapView and api/geocode.js now import the shared module,
and the two test suites merged into shared/__tests__/geocode.test.js —
the src/ copy was a strict subset of the server/ one. Added
`shared/**/*.js` to the coverage include list so the new directory is
held to the same per-file bar, and refreshed the CLAUDE.md architecture
section (which also still claimed api/geocode.js gates on cookie
presence rather than decrypting the session).

Tests:
Pure move — no behavior change. `npx vitest run --coverage`: 23 files,
219 tests passing, shared/geocode.js at 93.5% statements / 100%
branches / 100% functions, above the per-file thresholds.
